avoid_supplements.name: Aspirin
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Both are NSAIDs; combined use increases risk of GI bleeding, ulceration, and renal impairment
avoid_supplements.action: Do not combine ketorolac with aspirin or other NSAIDs without explicit physician approval

avoid_supplements.name: Warfarin or other anticoagulants
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Ketorolac inhibits platelet function and increases bleeding risk; may displace warfarin from protein binding
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; if necessary, monitor INR closely and adjust warfarin dose

avoid_supplements.name: Garlic (high-dose supplements)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Garlic has antiplatelet and anticoagulant properties; combined effect increases bleeding risk
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue high-dose garlic supplements during ketorolac therapy

avoid_supplements.name: Ginkgo biloba
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Ginkgo has antiplatelet effects; combined with ketorolac increases bleeding risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid ginkgo biloba supplements during ketorolac use

avoid_supplements.name: Omega-3 fatty acids (high-dose)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: High-dose omega-3 supplements have antiplatelet effects; increases bleeding risk with NSAIDs
avoid_supplements.action: Limit omega-3 supplementation to dietary sources or low-dose supplements; monitor for bleeding

avoid_supplements.name: ACE inhibitors/ARBs
avoid_supplements.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce efficacy of antihypertensives and increase risk of acute kidney injury
avoid_supplements.action: Monitor blood pressure and renal function; alternative analgesics may be preferred

avoid_supplements.name: Lithium
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Ketorolac may increase lithium levels by reducing renal clearance, risking toxicity
avoid_supplements.action: Monitor lithium levels closely; consider alternative NSAID or analgesic

caution_supplements.name: Turmeric (curcumin)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Turmeric has mild antiplatelet properties; may slightly increase bleeding risk when combined
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for signs of bleeding; use moderate amounts only

caution_supplements.name: Ginger
caution_supplements.mechanism: Ginger has mild antiplatelet effects; may have additive effect with ketorolac
caution_supplements.action: Use ginger cautiously and monitor for excessive bleeding

caution_supplements.name: Vitamin E (high-dose >400 IU)
caution_supplements.mechanism: High-dose vitamin E has mild anticoagulant properties
caution_supplements.action: Limit vitamin E supplementation to standard dietary levels or <400 IU daily

avoid_foods.name: Alcohol
avoid_foods.mechanism: Alcohol increases GI irritation and bleeding risk; may enhance gastric ulceration caused by ketorolac
avoid_foods.action: Avoid alcohol consumption during ketorolac therapy

caution_foods.name: High-salt foods
caution_foods.mechanism: NSAIDs impair renal sodium handling; high sodium intake may increase fluid retention and hypertension
caution_foods.action: Maintain moderate sodium intake; monitor blood pressure

caution_foods.name: Spicy foods
caution_foods.mechanism: Spicy foods may irritate GI mucosa, potentially increasing ulcer risk with NSAIDs
caution_foods.action: Limit spicy foods; take ketorolac with food to minimize GI irritation

caution_foods.name: Caffeine
caution_foods.mechanism: Caffeine may enhance analgesic effects but can increase GI irritation
caution_foods.action: Moderate caffeine consumption; take ketorolac with food and water

monitoring_notes: Monitor renal function (creatinine, BUN), blood pressure, and signs of GI bleeding. Ketorolac is contraindicated in severe renal impairment, advanced liver disease, or perioperative cardiac surgery. Educate patient on short-term use only (maximum 5 days) and increased cardiovascular and GI risks with prolonged use.
